search._reranker_comment: Optional cross-encoder reranker. After RRF fusion, the top N candidates are re-scored by a small cross-encoder (~80MB, ~50ms per query on CPU) that LOOKS AT chunk content vs query — fixing many 'top result is technically relevant but not the best answer' failures. Disabled by default to keep startup zero-cost; enable for production-grade quality.

_tools_comment: Which MCP tools `lynx serve` registers: core (5), standard (10, the default) or full (17). Every tool definition sits in the client's context on every turn, so smaller is cheaper. `include` / `exclude` adjust a profile by tool name; `lynx serve --profile` and the LYNX_TOOL_PROFILE variable override this block.

myproject._graph_comment: Opt-in knowledge graph layer (call graph + import graph + inheritance graph + community detection). Set enabled=true to expose the graph_query MCP tool (operations: callers, callees, subclasses, superclasses, imports, neighbors, shortest_path, overview, surprising_connections, status). Default is disabled — pure search still works without it.

exampleDocs_remove_or_replace._comment: Webdoc example — uncomment and adapt the URL to crawl a public docs site. Run `lynx build --source <name>` to fetch + index, again whenever you want a refresh (never automatic).
exampleDocs_remove_or_replace._render_comment: For SPA / client-side-rendered sites set render_js=true: pages load in headless Chromium so JS runs before extraction. Requires the webdoc-js extra (`lynx manager install webdoc-js`, downloads Chromium ~150MB). Slower per page — keep it off for server-rendered sites. render_wait_until: load | domcontentloaded | networkidle.

examplePdfs_remove_or_replace._comment: PDF example — point at a folder of .pdf files (manuals, RFCs, white-papers, ...). Lynx extracts text page-by-page and indexes one chunk per page; the AI client cites with `pdf_name p.42`. Scanned PDFs (no text layer) are auto-skipped; password-protected too. Watcher is OFF by default because re-extraction is costly; trigger refresh via `lynx build --source <name>`. For richer extraction on multi-column PDFs install pymupdf via `lynx manager install pdf-fast` and set extractor.backend="pymupdf" (or leave "auto").
